purpose: BigImage is a 3D Slicer extension for viewing very large whole-slide microscopy images (using tiffslide) and for H&E stain decomposition and nucleus segmentation (C++ CLIs). It also has a hidden Zarr reader/writer module. It is aimed at computational pathology users.
summary: The source has no signs of malicious behavior, network transmission, or unsafe execution. The main problem is environmental. BigImageViewer.py runs `pip_install("tiffslide")` at module top level, so a package install can happen when Slicer loads the module, without user consent. Other issues are lower severity. NgffImageIO has bugs (undefined `key` in the attribute loop, and `canLoadFile` always returns True). BigImageViewer has dead or broken code paths (`numpy.float`, an undefined Keras model, and CLI parameters that are not in the XML). The widget makes global changes in its constructor and never removes its interactor observers. The catalog entry uses `scm_revision: main`, a moving branch, so I could not review a pinned commit. The license is the Slicer BSD-style license, which is acceptable.
